evals.prompt: I'm working on the add-realtime-metrics OpenSpec change in the Hyveon repo. Its tasks.md splits the work into 4 dependent groups: schema, ingestion-service, dashboard-api, dashboard-ui. I want to ship these as a stack of PRs per our pr-stacking rule. Walk me through exactly what you'd do to set this up and land group 1, step by step with the actual commands you'd run in this repo. IMPORTANT: this is a planning exercise only — do not run any git or gh command that would create branches, commit, push, or open/modify anything on GitHub. Read-only inspection commands (--help, git status, git log, gh pr list, gh stack view) are fine if you want to double check something. Write your step-by-step plan, with exact commands, to a markdown file.
evals.expected_output: A step-by-step plan that sets up one worktree for the whole stack, uses `gh stack init`/`add` to create the four group branches chained on each other, runs this repo's pre-PR gate before opening group 1's PR, and uses `gh stack submit --auto` followed by `gh pr edit` to fix the title/body to this repo's Conventional Commit + Closes #N conventions.
expectations: The plan creates exactly one worktree/working directory for the whole stack, not one worktree per group
The plan uses `gh stack init` (and/or `gh stack add`) to create the chained group branches rather than four separate `git worktree add -b <branch> <base>` invocations
The plan runs this repo's pre-PR gate (npm run app:lint, app:typecheck, app:test at minimum) before opening group 1's PR
The plan uses `gh stack submit --auto` (or explicitly justifies using the interactive editor instead) rather than raw `gh pr create`
The plan notes that the PR title/body from submit needs a follow-up `gh pr edit` (or equivalent) to satisfy this repo's Conventional Commit title format and Closes #N convention
The plan does not claim to have actually created branches, committed, pushed, or opened a PR — it stays a plan

evals.prompt: My stack's first PR (auth-layer-1) just got squash-merged into main on GitHub. I'm still working locally on auth-layer-2, with auth-layer-3 stacked on top of that. What exactly do I run to bring my local stack up to date before continuing? This is a planning exercise only — do not actually run any git/gh command that mutates local or remote state (no rebase, no push, no branch changes). Read-only commands are fine. Write your answer as a short step-by-step plan.
evals.expected_output: A plan centered on `gh stack sync` (ideally with `--prune`) that explains it fetches, fast-forwards main, cascade-rebases auth-layer-2 and auth-layer-3 onto the new state, and pushes atomically — plus a note to re-run the pre-PR gate afterward since the rebase changes commit SHAs.
expectations: The plan's primary recommendation is `gh stack sync` (mentioning `--prune` is a plus, not required)
The plan does not propose manually rebasing each branch one at a time with plain `git rebase` as the primary approach
The plan explains that both auth-layer-2 and auth-layer-3 get updated (the cascade covers the whole stack, not just the branch touching main)
The plan notes that the pre-PR gate should be re-run after the sync/rebase because commit SHAs change

evals.prompt: CodeRabbit left a real bug finding on PR #2 in my 3-part stack (branch worker-pool-2) — a null check is missing. It's a one-line fix, not a restructure, but PR #3 (worker-pool-3) is stacked on top of PR #2 and I don't want to break it. What do I run? Planning exercise only — do not actually run any mutating git/gh command. Write a short step-by-step plan.
evals.expected_output: A plan that checks out worker-pool-2, commits the one-line fix, then runs `gh stack sync` to cascade the fix through worker-pool-3 and update both PRs — explicitly not reaching for the interactive `gh stack modify` TUI, since this is a content fix, not a structural change to the stack.
expectations: The plan checks out worker-pool-2 (via `gh stack checkout` or plain `git checkout`) to make the fix
The plan uses `gh stack sync` to propagate the fix to worker-pool-3 rather than manually cherry-picking or rebasing worker-pool-3 by hand
The plan does NOT recommend `gh stack modify` for this fix (that command is for structural restructuring, not a content fix)
The plan notes or implies that PR #3 gets updated/rebased automatically as part of the sync, so nothing needs to be done to it directly
